'2005 new panel': grade-11 students newly sampled in 2005 (cohort NP) and surveyed with the core panel in 2005 and 2007 (TEPS English overview, sampling design).

expression:
local({
  rel <- case_when(
    .wave == "1" ~ as.numeric(w1p101),
    .wave == "2" ~ as.numeric(w2p101),
    .wave == "3" ~ as.numeric(w3p101),
    .wave == "4" ~ as.numeric(w4p102)
  )
  sex <- case_when(
    .wave == "1" ~ as.numeric(w1p102),
    .wave == "2" ~ as.numeric(w2p102),
    .wave == "3" ~ as.numeric(w3p102),
    .wave == "4" ~ as.numeric(w4p101)
  )
  case_when(
    is.na(rel) ~ NA_character_,
    rel %in% 1:3 & sex %in% 2 ~ "Mother",
    rel %in% 1:3 & sex %in% 1 ~ "Father",
    rel %in% 4:6 ~ "Other carer",
    .default = "Unknown"
  )
})
notes: Parent questionnaire at each wave: 'What is your relationship with this student?' (parent, step-parent, foster or adoptive parent, grandparent, elder brother or sister, other) and the respondent's gender. A parent, step-parent or foster or adoptive parent: female = Mother, male = Father; grandparent, elder sibling or other = Other carer; relationship or gender missing or illegal = Unknown; no parent questionnaire record = NA. W3 releases labels for code 1 of both items only; its codes are read with the W1, W2 and W4 options, which the study's fully labelled W3 mother variables confirm (w3mowork equals the respondent's own employment for every code-2 parent and the spouse's for every code-1 parent, and is missing for relationship codes 4-6). Screen time is self-reported, so this is the main parent questionnaire's respondent. Not carried.

Survey year minus birth year, plus the fieldwork midpoint as a year fraction minus 0.5: midpoint as a decimal year (2001-12-01, 2003-04-09, 2005-12-01, 2007-05-16 from the user guides) minus mid-birth-year. birth_year comes from the tidier: the ROC-year labels of w1s501 (J, S and core panel, carried from W1) or w3s479 (NP, carried to W4) + 1911. w3s479's codes 1-5 are relabelled ROC 75-79 in the tidier: the released labels (ROC 71-75) would make 2005 grade-11 students 20-21, and the codes match the core panel's ROC 77-78 four codes down (NP mean age 16.85 at W3, core panel 16.80).

notes: Student report, multiple choice: 'From childhood to now, which languages do your parents commonly use when talking with you at home?' Mandarin alone = Country language only; Mandarin with another = Country language and another; others without Mandarin = Another language only; no option ticked = Unknown. Carried within participant (carry-forward rule), so core-panel W1, W2 and W4 rows and new-panel W3 rows take the reported value; the rest of the 2001 samples were never asked: Unknown. Proximate: the languages the parents commonly speak with the child, not every language spoken in the home. The language-fluency items (student w1s5051-w1s5056, w3s3311-w3s3316; parent w1p108-w1p113) are proficiency and not used.
